verdict.rationale: Sift documents Workflows as a rules automation platform for making real-time, risk-based decisions during key events, with custom Workflows, custom Decisions, abuse-specific risk scores and Review Queues. That covers authoring rules on model scores that route to block or review outcomes. However, the evidence never shows rule conditions built on velocity counters, list matches or arbitrary transaction attributes. An old CEO remark that the product had 'no rules' predates the documented Workflows feature, so it does not concretely contradict current docs and only lowers confidence. Missing for 10: documented velocity-counter conditions, list/allowlist/blocklist matching in rules, explicit transaction-attribute conditions, a description of the rule-authoring logic (AND/OR combinations), and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a risk analyst, I can author custom rules that combine model scores, velocity counters, list matches, and transaction attributes into allow, block, or review decisions

citations.quote: Sift offers Workflows, a powerful rules automation platform, and Review Queues.
Workflows enable you to make risk-based decisions in real time during key events. Follow this guide to create your own custom Workflow.
Learn to set up custom Decisions, like Ban Account or Cancel Order, that are connected to real business actions in your backend.
Learn how to add an abuse-specific risk score so that you can easily do so.
